description: Conformance corpus for object key order across the host boundary. A host object keeps the order its keys were written in, in both directions and when a hook payload spreads to arguments. Every key set here is deliberately out of code-point order. The JavaScript and C# runtimes keep authored order natively; the Rust runtime keeps it when built with its `preserve_order` cargo feature, and runs this corpus only then.
notes: `inbound`: the binding `value` returns `hostValue`; the runtime executes `(function () { var v = value(); return (<probe>); })()` and the result must equal `expected`.
`echo`: the binding `echo` returns, as an array, the arguments it received. The runtime executes `script` and the result must equal `expected`.

`hook`: the setup script registers `hooks.probe(function () { return Array.prototype.join.call(arguments, ','); })`, then the host fires `probe` with `data` as its single payload value; the one result must equal `expected`. A Rust host fires it as `fire_hook("probe", &[data])`.

echo.description: Returns the arguments it received, as an array.

probe.description: Reports the arguments its handlers receive.

inbound.name: a host object keeps its key order
a nested object keeps its key order
inbound.probe: (function () { var keys = []; for (var k in v.outer) keys.push(k); return keys.join(','); })()

inbound.name: unusual keys keep JavaScript's own key order

echo.name: a script object round-trips in authored order
echo.script: (function () { var r = echo({ x: 1, a: 2 }); return Object.keys(r[0]).join(','); })()

echo.name: unusual keys round-trip in JavaScript's own key order
echo.script: (function () { var o = {}; o[''] = 1; o['\u0000'] = 2; o['\uD83D\uDE00'] = 3; o['4294967295'] = 4; o['-1'] = 5; o['01'] = 6; o['4294967294'] = 7; var r = echo(o)[0]; return JSON.stringify(Object.keys(r)) + '|' + Object.keys(r).map(function (k) { return r[k]; }).join(','); })()

hook.name: a payload object spreads in authored order
